title: Instrument audit events for model deployment + rollout actions (canary, pin/unpin, fallback policy)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Context
- We need 100% audit log coverage for sensitive actions. Model deployment and rollout controls are explicitly in-scope (enterprise questionnaires call this out as “production change management”).
- This ticket covers instrumentation for actions across Console + controllers:
  - canary start/stop
  - pin/unpin model versions
  - fallback policy changes (incl. automatic fallback enable/disable and preferred fallback target)

Scope
In scope actions/events (schema v1)
1) Canary
- Start canary rollout for a deployment
- Stop/abort canary rollout
- Promote canary to stable (if applicable in our rollout controller)

2) Version pinning
- Pin deployment to a model version / artifact
- Unpin (return to “latest compatible” tracking)

3) Fallback policy
- Update fallback policy for deployment (policy enable/disable; list/ordering of fallback targets; region fallback)

Out of scope (this ticket)
- Per-request runtime routing events (non-sensitive, too high volume)
- Non-admin read operations (list deployments, view status)
- Dedicated capacity scaling (ENG-2486)
- Legacy event backfill beyond dual-write mapping (ENG-2490)

Event naming (final)
Per naming guidelines + Slack architecture decision, use “deployments.*” namespace for control plane rollout actions.
- deployments.canary.started
- deployments.canary.stopped
- deployments.canary.promoted
- deployments.version.pinned
- deployments.version.unpinned
- deployments.fallback_policy.updated

Required fields (must pass schema v1 validator)
- event_version: "1"
- event_name: as above
- occurred_at: RFC3339
- org_id, workspace_id (if applicable)
- actor: type + id + display_name (and service identity when controller-initiated)
- target: deployment_id + deployment_name + model_id/model_name (where applicable)
- request_id (propagate from Console/API gateway where user initiated)
- ip_address + user_agent (when actor is end-user; omit/NULL for service actor)
- outcome: success|failure
- error: present on failure with stable error_code

Actor attribution requirements
- If initiated from Console/API: actor.type=user; actor.id=user_id; include request_id from gateway.
- If initiated by controller automation (e.g., rollback/auto-promote): actor.type=service; actor.id=service principal (e.g., "runtime-rollout-controller"); ALSO include actor.on_behalf_of when there is a directly responsible user action (e.g., user configured policy that triggers later automation). If no on-behalf-of, leave blank and include reason in audit payload.

Payload expectations (redaction-safe)
- Include before/after for all “update” style operations:
  - deployments.fallback_policy.updated: before/after policy summary (no secrets)
  - deployments.version.pinned: before/after resolved version
- Include rollout identifiers:
  - deployment_rollout_id
  - canary_percent / traffic_split (when applicable)
- Never include tokens, credentials, raw prompts, or customer data.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] All listed actions emit audit events with schema v1 envelope and pass validation in staging.
- [x] request_id correlation works end-to-end for user initiated actions (Console -> API -> control plane -> audit pipeline).
- [x] Actor attribution matches reality for controller initiated operations; no “user=unknown” events.
- [x] Fallback policy updates include before/after, redacted.
- [x] Dual-write mapping to legacy event names included where we already had partial/legacy audit logs (coordinate with ENG-2490).
- [x] Unit tests for each event emitter + integration coverage via audit harness (ENG-2492).

Implementation notes
- Use shared audit lib + registry (ENG-2482) and JSONSchema definitions (ENG-2481).
- Emit events at the point of state mutation (control plane service), not in the UI.
- For canary start/stop/promote, instrumentation lives in rollout-controller handler methods; ensure we capture the diff before mutating.
- On failure: emit audit event with outcome=failure only when we can strongly attribute the attempted action (e.g., authorization passed but mutation failed). Do NOT emit for unauthenticated/unknown callers; instead rely on API gateway security logs.

Links
- PR (implementation): sources/github/redwood/pr_18479.json
- Naming conventions: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/audit-event-naming-guidelines.json
- Schema v1: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-event-schema-v1.json
- Actor attribution discussion: sources/slack/eng-runtime/thread_1717684410.json
comments: 2025-05-24 (Marcus Lin): Please ensure “fallback policy change” is treated as sensitive. We’ve seen customers require evidence for any change that can impact availability or data routing. Add before/after and a stable error_code on failure.

2025-05-27 (Allison Grant): +1 on emitting at the mutation layer. Also, we should avoid emitting both “started” and “updated” for the same operation unless product wants that. Keep event taxonomy minimal and stable.

2025-05-29 (Diego Santos): Drafted event names under deployments.*. Open question: do we need separate events for “auto rollback happened” vs “user stopped canary”? Proposal: canary.stopped includes payload.reason=user_request|auto_rollback and actor.type=service for automation.

2025-05-30 (Naomi Feldman): Agree on single canary.stopped event with reason. Make sure this aligns with enterprise FAQ wording (customers care that it’s captured, not necessarily split into two events).

2025-06-03 (Chloe Martin): Request_id propagation: Console -> control plane already carries x-request-id; rollout controller needs to keep it when it spawns async work. Please add a field for “parent_request_id” if work gets detached.

2025-06-04 (Diego Santos): Implemented parent_request_id in payload only (not schema field) to avoid schema changes. request_id remains the original inbound id when available; for fully async controller actions we generate a new request_id and record parent_request_id in payload for traceability.
2025-06-07 (Marcus Lin): Redaction reminder: no full policy JSON if it contains customer-specific endpoints. Summarize to policy_id + enabled + ordered list of fallback target deployment_ids.

2025-06-12 (Diego Santos): PR up. Added before/after snapshots for pin/unpin + fallback policy update. Canary events include rollout_id, traffic_split, and reason field. Waiting on review from Telemetry for outcome/error semantics.

2025-06-14 (Nadia Rahman): Reviewed. Outcome semantics look good. Please ensure error_code is stable (enum) not raw exception string. Also add a small unit test asserting validation fails if actor is missing.
2025-06-17 (Diego Santos): Addressed feedback: standardized error_code (DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_DENIED, VALIDATION_FAILED, INTERNAL). Added unit tests and wired to validator. Merged.
2025-06-19 (Connor O'Brien): Verified in staging with audit harness: canary start/stop and pin/unpin present + searchable. Marking Done.
